title: བསྟན་འགྱུར། སྡེ་དགེ། ཚད་མ། དེ (Derge Tengyur, vol. 180)
shelf_note: Pramāṇa commentary (a Pramāṇavārttika-type commentary refuting Īśvara and pradhāna as creators), correctly shelved in the Derge Tengyur Tshad ma section.

ocr_errors.problem: བྱེ་བྲག (difference) misread as བྲེ་བྲག; meaning recoverable

ocr_errors.image: འདོད་ཆགས་ལ་སོགས་པ་དང་ལྡན་ཡང་ (as far as I can read the print)
ocr_errors.problem: ལྡན 'endowed with' read as ལན 'reply'. This changes the root-text lemma, and translation A carries the error ('the reply concerning attachment')

tr_errors_A.english: why would he engage in the conventional activities of ignorant wandering beings?
tr_errors_A.problem: drops མེད་པའི ('of the non-existent') and makes Īśvara the one who engages, where the text says he causes ignorant beings to engage; the point of the quoted objection is blurred

tr_errors_A.english: Also with respect to the reply concerning attachment and so forth...
tr_errors_A.problem: follows the OCR misreading ལན 'reply'; the image reads 'even though endowed with attachment etc.'

tr_errors_A.english: teaching their antidotes does not conflict with Īśvara himself; nevertheless, it is improper because it is not preceded by intellect
tr_errors_A.problem: restructures the objection and adds 'nevertheless'; the reason clause is attached to the wrong verb, though the objector's overall claim survives
keywords list terms that do not appear on the page

tr_errors_B.english: are simply anything compatible with the subject
tr_errors_B.problem: 'either the paksha or the sapakṣa' (thesis or similar instance) is collapsed into 'compatible with the subject'; the disjunction is lost

tr_errors_B.english: how can it be understood through karma?
tr_errors_B.problem: the question is how karma is inferred (karma is the object of the inference), not how something is known 'through karma'. The roles are swapped

tr_errors_B.english: the observation of various results ... leads to an analysis. If a creator Lord possesses compassion and similar qualities
tr_errors_B.problem: རྣམ་པར་དཔྱོད་པ ('discernment', one of Īśvara's attributes) is read as 'leads to an analysis', so it drops out of the list of attributes. The same word is also rendered 'analysis' later

pages.prefer_reason: Neither has a serious error. A is right on the logic of the opening (paksha or sapakṣa; karma as what is inferred; discernment as Īśvara's attribute), while B mis-parses all three; A's one OCR-driven slip ('reply') matters less.

book_verdict: The right leaf, with a good transcription: one meaning-relevant misread (ལན for ལྡན). Both translations are usable; A is somewhat more faithful to the argument.
